answer: A registry can tie each agent to a verifiable work history, like a coastline of receipts: every payment, delivery, and dispute leaves a public trace, so a fake identity starts with nothing. When a gale of new accounts appears, the network checks whether each one has earned trust through completed jobs, collateral, or endorsements from established agents, rather than self-declared credentials. New agents begin in a meadow of low-stakes tasks and only graduate to valuable work after consistent, auditable performance, while an ocean of cheap clones cannot borrow reputation they never earned.
